beats: Hook (p4): write a five-qubit program once and run it on a dozen chips with different wiring and different native gates; what has to happen in between, and in what order? (line_qc_pass_one_sheet_many_chips, then tape p4). Cast for all of QC03 (lecture Q25-03), the same in every part: the planner = the compiler (two short braids, round glasses, utility vest); the fabricator = the chip maker (bald, walrus moustache, goggles, work apron); the programmer = the person who writes the program (tall, wavy hair, long scarf, backpack); the four guests told apart by their hats (beret, beanie, top hat, flat cap) = the program's qubits; a chip tile = a square tile of studs (qubits) joined by bars (couplings).

Her frame (p2-p3, clip 02:07-02:32): research problems come from hardware limits: the whole system is noisy, it speaks only a few native gates, its qubits have few connections; every pass of the compiler answers one limit (line_qc_pass_sofa_door: the doorway is the limit, the sofa is the program).

Two goals (p5, 04:39-05:46; tape p5): write once, run on many chips; and optimise for fidelity (reuse line_qc_pass_one_sheet_many_chips with red-pen rings). Compilers are modular, a set of passes (clip 06:23-06:48).

Pass 1, unroll (p6, 06:23-08:00): break every bigger gate into one- and two-qubit gates, a matrix decomposition that computes exactly the same thing (line_qc_pass_sofa_pieces: the same sofa, in pieces that fit through the door, put back together inside).

Pass 2, initial layout (p6): place the program's qubits on good physical qubits, or on densely linked ones, using calibration data when there is some (line_qc_pass_good_chairs: skip the broken chairs, seat the pair that talks side by side).
Pass 3, extend with ancillas (p7): the unused physical qubits join the layout as spare places (the empty laid places at the end of line_qc_pass_good_chairs).
Pass 4, insert SWAPs (p7): a two-qubit gate needs neighbours; when two qubits sit apart, SWAPs move them together (line_qc_pass_seat_swap; QC02-04 and QC02-05 told the routing story in full).

Pass 5, translate to the native basis (p8, 10:54-11:46): rewrite everything in the few gates the chip calibrates; several optimisation passes follow (line_qc_pass_two_tools: a whole chair built with the only two tools on the wall).

Every pass is driven by a limitation of the hardware (clip 11:46-12:12; reuse line_mic for the clip tag). The slides p6-p8 are source-code screenshots: redraw the pass list as lettering. Check first: today's Qiskit preset pass manager names its stages init, layout, routing, translation, optimization, scheduling; the slide links an older level3.py.

Open questions (Q24-02 p8): a better pass, the order of the passes, and co-design across passes (line_qc_pass_carpet_paint: rug first, ceiling second, and the order hurts). Bridge: QC03-02 is a case where two passes have to decide together.
Cover (line_qc_cover_03_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the programmer hands one blank sheet to the planner, who looks at a row of differently wired chip tiles.
